results.label: logistic · split by prompt
results.summary: At the reference operating point (threshold chosen in advance to route about half the prompts cheap, not tuned on the outcome), the router sends 59% of prompts to the cheap configuration, reaching 69.0% accuracy at $0.509 per 1M prompts (23% below always-expensive, which scores 70.8%). A random mix at the SAME average cost reaches 68.2%, so the router beats random mixing by +0.8 points. An oracle at that cost would reach 71.9%, leaving 2.9 points of headroom that no router built from these features captured. The best threshold found anywhere on the sweep gains +0.8 points at 59% routed cheap, but that threshold was selected on the data it is scored on and is optimistic. This is an OFFLINE simulation replayed over logged benchmark outputs; it does not show that the router would work on real traffic or in a live serving system.

results.summary: At the reference operating point (threshold chosen in advance to route about half the prompts cheap, not tuned on the outcome), the router sends 49% of prompts to the cheap configuration, reaching 68.5% accuracy at $0.534 per 1M prompts (19% below always-expensive, which scores 70.8%). A random mix at the SAME average cost reaches 68.6%, so the router does NOT beat random mixing (-0.2 points). An oracle at that cost would reach 71.9%, leaving 3.5 points of headroom that no router built from these features captured. The best threshold found anywhere on the sweep gains +0.1 points at 98% routed cheap, but that threshold was selected on the data it is scored on and is optimistic. This is an OFFLINE simulation replayed over logged benchmark outputs; it does not show that the router would work on real traffic or in a live serving system.
